name: SiteHold – Coming Soon & Maintenance Mode
author: ruhulamin77777

sections.description:
SiteHold shows visitors a clean, responsive Coming Soon or Maintenance page while you build or fix your site. Administrators keep seeing the real site.

Features

  • Three modes: Off, Coming Soon (HTTP 200) and Maintenance (HTTP 503 + Retry-After, SEO safe)
  • One-click switch in the admin top bar, with a coloured status indicator
  • Countdown timer with optional automatic go-live
  • Logo, background image, overlay, text and accent colours
  • Separate headline and message for each mode
  • Contact button and social links (Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube)
  • Secret bypass link to share with clients — no login needed
  • Allow selected user roles and IP addresses to see the live site
  • Exclude specific pages (e.g. /privacy-policy or /landing/*)
  • Optional REST API blocking
  • Page title, meta description and noindex control
  • Preview without turning the mode on
  • Tells caching plugins not to cache the holding page
  • Translation ready, clean uninstall
sections.installation:
1. Upload the sitehold folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings → SiteHold, choose a mode and customise your page.
  4. Use the SiteHold item in the admin top bar to switch modes at any time.
sections.faq:
I enabled it but I still see my site.

You are logged in as an administrator, who always sees the live site. Open your site in a private window or use the Preview buttons.

Which mode should I use?

Use Coming Soon for a site that has not launched yet. Use Maintenance for short downtime — it sends a 503 status so search engines don’t drop your pages.

I still see the page after turning it off.

Clear your caching plugin / CDN cache.

Can I use my own template?

Yes. Use the sitehold_template filter to return the path of your own PHP template.
